chunks: From him, from al-Qasim, from Aban, from Mansur, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who made an oath of abstention from his wife, and four months passed with her. He said: He is suspended. If he decides on divorce, she becomes divorced from him, and she has the waiting period of the divorced woman. If not, he expiates his oath, and he keeps her.

key_terms.إِيلَاء: Oath of abstention from conjugal relations
key_terms.عِدَّةُ الْمُطَلَّقَةِ: The waiting period of the divorced woman

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a husband takes an oath to abstain from his wife for four months?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the procedural timeline for 'ila', specifying that the four-month period is a waiting phase rather than an automatic divorce. It highlights the juristic distinction between 'ila' and 'zihar' by mandating that if the husband remains silent after the term, he must perform kaffarah (expiation) to resume relations, whereas explicit declaration results in a final divorce with the corresponding 'iddah'. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the husband's active choice and the financial/spiritual cost of breaking the marital bond through oath.
